decision_reason: The NASA Marshall catalog and a NASA conference presentation identify this exact multi-Doppler analysis toolkit, and the repo has a NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 grant for the NASA software plus a separate University of Oklahoma BSD-style grant for the DDA component. However, the repo explicitly says MultiDop has been superseded by PyDDA and recommends using PyDDA; there is no current product-specific use signal for this source. Hold pending a decision that its historical significance clears the baseline's Archived exception.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies this exact software under designation MFS-33436-1; the repository license identifies NASA Marshall Space Flight Center as the government originator.

public_source.note: Public Python/C source, setup instructions, and Jupyter examples are available. README states the package has been superseded and recommends PyDDA instead.

eligible_license.note: The attached grant is NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 for the NASA MultiDop work (MFS-33436-1); the adjacent CIMMS/University of Oklahoma document separately grants BSD-style rights for the original DDA C component. Do not collapse the two scopes.

primary_evidence.note: NASA NTRS record and conference presentation identify MultiDop and its multi-radar wind-analysis purpose; NASA TTP provides the exact release. Current use/parity is not established, which is why disposition remains hold.

product_identity: Multiple-Doppler Radar Analysis Toolkit (MultiDop), NASA MSFC Python interface and analysis workflow over University of Oklahoma DDA and Py-ART; distinct from successor PyDDA
agency: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (NASA-developed interface; DDA C component by University of Oklahoma/CIMMS)
geography: United States federal meteorology and radar-science research
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 for NASA's MultiDop release; University of Oklahoma/CIMMS BSD-style license for the original DDA C component
status_note: Hold: stale source and repo README explicitly recommends PyDDA. NASA's catalog card still exists, but does not prove current use of this superseded source. Consider Archived only if the historic-significance exception is accepted.

decision_reason: NASA Glenn released this documented toolbox of MPTCP analysis tools, scripts, and configurations and NASA reports identify its exact use in network/flight experiments. The repository is public, has a NOSA 1.3 grant naming designation LEW-19620-1, and source activity continues in 2026. Treat all internal modules as one NASA-released toolkit; the Linux kernel-patch targets and separately used networking software retain their own licenses.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies the exact Multipath TCP (MPTCP) Tools, Analytics, and Configurations product and describes its use for multi-interface satellite/optical links; the root NOSA names NASA Glenn Research Center.

public_source.note: Public repository includes network traffic analysis applications, MPTCP-over-PPP experiment configurations, UDP proxy, and kernel patches with usage docs and source; packaged releases are referenced in the README.

eligible_license.note: The root grant is NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.3 and names NASA Glenn and designation LEW-19620-1. It applies to NASA-authored subject software; Linux kernel and other third-party components remain under their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: NASA Glenn's report describes the MPTCP tooling suite in the context of flight/network experiments and planned release; the current NASA TTP page identifies the exact tools/configurations product and its tested NASA Earth Science project use.

product_identity: Multipath TCP (MPTCP) Tools, Analytics, and Configurations: one NASA Glenn collection of network-analysis applications, experiment configurations, proxy, and kernel patches
geography: United States federal flight-networking and Earth-science communications research
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 for NASA Glenn's LEW-19620-1 collection; embedded Linux kernel patches, target kernels, and external dependencies remain under their own applicable licenses
status_note: Maintained: repository has source-level activity into 2026 and NASA TTP still distributes the exact toolbox. NASA's technical report documents the tool components and test-flight/network-analysis context.

decision_reason: This repository is a collection of 3D models, textures, and images, not a software product or source-code repository. Some assets have third-party contributors and the README points to asset usage guidelines; it should not be admitted as a government OSS software project.

government_provenance.note: NASA's repository README identifies the multi-center NASA contributors and contact route for the 3D-asset collection.

public_source.note: The repository tree contains 3D models, 3D-printing files, images, textures, and metadata; no software source code or runnable software product is present.

eligible_license.note: README says assets are free and without copyright but directs users to separate usage guidelines; this asset rights statement is not a software license and contributors include external organizations.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party NASA description explicitly defines the repository as a growing collection of 3D models, textures, and images rather than a software product.

product_identity: NASA 3D Resources asset collection (3D models, textures, images), not software
geography: United States federal space-science education and outreach
license: Not applicable as a software product; individual assets follow applicable NASA usage guidelines and contributor rights

decision_reason: The public repository contains a NASA acronyms web-data/browser tool and an MIT grant; its README names NASA.gov contacts and says it was moved to NASA's official GitHub. However, the user-facing service is a separate nasaacronyms.com deployment (not a NASA.gov service); its HTML has not changed since 2021 and the official NASA acronym pages/internal Acronym Central are separate systems. Hold pending primary evidence that NASA currently operates or sponsors this exact deployed product and that its service/source parity remains current.

government_provenance.note: NASA-hosted repository and README with NASA employee contact and migration note are leads, but no official NASA.gov page was found that identifies nasaacronyms.com as an agency product; NASA's own Acronym Central/public glossary are separate services.

public_source.note: Public repository contains acronym data and app/browser-extension code; the live service CSP points to the NASA repository's current raw acronym JSON.

eligible_license.note: MIT_License.txt contains the full standard MIT grant and states NASA copyright; this applies to the repository source, not third-party browser extensions or the external web deployment as a whole.

primary_evidence.note: Live non-government domain operates the acronym lookup and CSP/data endpoint ties it to the repository, but its static HTML was last modified 2021 and no current official NASA service/support page confirms agency operation or exact UI source parity. The NASA-hosted Acronym Central referenced elsewhere is a different service.

product_identity: NASA Acronyms, a searchable NASA acronym data/browser lookup tool linked to the separate nasaacronyms.com website; relationship to official NASA acronym services is unresolved
geography: United States federal space-science information reference
license: MIT for the NASA-Acronyms repository source; deployment platform, third-party JS/browser-extension code, and acronym content are not covered absent explicit inclusion
status_note: Hold: repository is public and data is refreshed through 2026, but site HTML has a 2021 last-modified date and agency stewardship/source parity for the non-.gov deployment are unverified.

decision_reason: NASA publishes NASA-LaTeX-Docs as an SRA-approved software project and its current user documentation covers an OS-independent Python build tool and reusable NASA/AIAA templates. The root project grant began as NOSA 1.3 in 2017 and changed to MIT in 2020; current LICENSE and code.nasa.gov list the exact project as MIT. Source updates continue in 2026.

government_provenance.note: NASA's official code.nasa.gov portal labels itself a catalog of NASA code that received Software Release Authority approval and lists this exact repository. The 2017 NASA OSA identifies NASA as the originating agency.

public_source.note: Public repository includes the Python PDF build script, reusable document templates, and support files; project documentation explains requirements and user workflows.

eligible_license.note: Current root LICENSE is the standard MIT License (NASA copyright, 2020). Its earlier root grant was NOSA 1.3, added in a source-bearing 2017 commit; code.nasa.gov also identifies current MIT status.

primary_evidence.note: Official project docs include a quick start, Python/LaTeX requirements, template-specific guidance, and generated outputs; NASA code.nasa.gov lists the exact reusable software project.

product_identity: NASA-LaTeX-Docs, reusable LaTeX templates and Python document-build tooling for technical reports, memos, and research papers
geography: United States federal technical documentation and research reporting
license: Current MIT License for NASA-LaTeX-Docs, preceded by a NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 grant first verified in 2017; separately installed TeX/LaTeX dependencies are not included
